bib.title: Evaluating the Factual Consistency of Abstractive Text Summarization

read.skipped: Appendix A example predictions skimmed only (qualitative examples)

question: Can a model trained on cheap synthetic data verify whether summary sentences are factually consistent with the source document, and explain why?
hypothesis: Weakly-supervised in-domain synthetic data beats strongly-supervised data from related tasks (NLI, fact checking) for factual consistency checking of fairly extractive summaries.
contributions: Weakly-supervised BERT-based factual consistency model (FactCC) trained on rule-based synthetic data
FactCCX with span extraction heads that explain the decision
Manually annotated CNN/DM validation and test set for factual consistency
Release of code for training data generation and model weights

method.summary: Sentences are sampled from CNN/DM articles and passed through rule-based transformations (paraphrase by backtranslation as positive; entity, number, pronoun swap, negation as negative; noise injection) to make about 1M labelled (document, claim) pairs. Uncased BERT-base is fine-tuned for binary CONSISTENT/INCONSISTENT classification (FactCC), and a variant adds span-selection heads (FactCCX). Evaluated on hand-annotated CNN/DM summaries and XSum summaries, and in a human study.
method.task: document-sentence factual consistency classification of summaries

datasets.name: Synthetic FactCC training data
datasets.source: generated from CNN/DailyMail (Nallapati et al., 2016) news articles
datasets.preprocessing: random sentence sampled per document as claim; transformations: paraphrase via backtranslation (French, German, Chinese, Spanish, Russian through Google Cloud Translation API), entity/number swap (SpaCy NER, random unique swap within group), pronoun swap, sentence negation, noise injection (per-token duplicate or drop with a preset probability; value not given)

datasets.name: CNN/DM annotated validation
datasets.source: summaries from ten published summarization systems, annotated by the authors

datasets.name: MNLI and FEVER
datasets.source: Williams et al. 2018; Thorne et al. 2018
datasets.preprocessing: neutral class removed from both, to train baseline BERT classifiers

datasets.name: Falke et al. (2019) sentence ranking test data

models.name: FactCC
models.architecture: BERT-base uncased with single-layer classifier on [CLS]

models.name: FactCCX
models.architecture: FactCC plus span selection heads (start/end indices) for source support span and claim error span

training.objective: two-way classification (CONSISTENT/INCONSISTENT); FactCCX adds span start/end supervision

metrics.name: F1 score
metrics.definition: F1 on the annotated test set

metrics.name: sentence pair ranking error
metrics.definition: percent of (positive, negative) claim pairs where the negative gets the higher correctness probability (Falke et al. 2019)

metrics.name: span helpfulness and overlap
metrics.definition: human-rated helpfulness; span accuracy = model span fully contained in human span; token F1 between spans

baselines: DA, InferSent, SSE, ESIM, BERT (Falke et al., 2019)
eval.protocol: Single run reported, no seeds or significance test stated. Human study: 100 examples from CNN/DM test, balanced between classes, 3 judges each from English-speaking countries.

availability.data: https://github.com/salesforce/factCC (annotated dataset and data generation code)

evidence.quote: Experiments were conducted on 8 Nvidia V100 GPUs, training took 23 hours on average.

limits: Transformations lack multi-sentence abstractive paraphrase, so FactCC loses to MNLI on XSum (authors state this was expected)
Misses commonsense errors, temporal inconsistencies and incorrect coreference
Test set annotated by the authors; crowdsourced annotation too noisy to use
Summary re-ranking experiment of Falke et al. could not be replicated
Single run, no seeds, optimizer, warmup, noise probability or XSum test size stated
Even with highlights, inter-annotator kappa is only 0.2526

terms.definition: a factually consistent summary contains only statements that are entailed by the source document
